Give an interview-style explanation of Recursion.

Recursion solves a problem by calling a function on smaller instances of the same problem. Time and space complexity depend on the recurrence and recursion depth. It is useful for tree traversal, divide-and-conquer, and backtracking.
What should a beginner know about Tree Traversal?
Tree traversal visits the nodes of a tree in a specified order. Standard traversals take O(n) time.
Explain Knapsack in simple words.
The 0/1 knapsack problem chooses items with weights and values under a capacity constraint, using each item at most once. It is useful for resource-allocation optimization.
What should a beginner know about Tabulation?
Tabulation computes dynamic-programming states iteratively in dependency order. Its time complexity depends on the number of states and transitions.
When should we use Two Pointers?
It is useful for sorted pair-sum problems and removing duplicates.
What is the time complexity associated with Dynamic Programming?
Complexity depends on the number of states and transitions.
What is Disjoint Set Union?
Disjoint Set Union maintains groups of elements using find and union operations.
Give a simple example of Binary Search Tree.
In a BST rooted at 8, values 4 and 12 can be placed on the left and right.
What is the time complexity associated with Dijkstra Algorithm?
With an adjacency list and binary heap, it typically takes O((V + E) log V).
What is the time complexity associated with Topological Sort?
It takes O(V + E) time with standard algorithms.
What is the time complexity associated with Kadane Algorithm?
Its time complexity is O(n) and auxiliary space can be O(1).
Give an interview-style explanation of Heap.
A heap is a complete binary tree that satisfies a heap-order property. Getting the root is O(1), and insertion and removal are O(log n). Heaps are useful for priority queues and top-k problems.
Give an interview-style explanation of Binary Search Tree.

A binary search tree orders keys so that left-subtree keys are smaller and right-subtree keys are larger, under the usual distinct-key convention. Search, insertion, and deletion take O(h), where h is the tree height. BSTs support ordered searching and traversal.
Explain Minimum Spanning Tree in simple words.
A minimum spanning tree connects all vertices of a connected weighted undirected graph with minimum total edge weight and no cycles. It is useful for designing low-cost networks.
Explain the main idea behind Minimum Spanning Tree.
A minimum spanning tree connects all vertices of a connected weighted undirected graph with minimum total edge weight and no cycles. It is useful for designing low-cost networks.

The 0/1 knapsack problem chooses items with weights and values under a capacity constraint, using each item at most once. The standard dynamic-programming solution takes O(nW) time, where W is capacity. It is useful for resource-allocation optimization.
What is Topological Sort?
Topological sorting orders the vertices of a directed acyclic graph so every edge goes from earlier to later.
Explain Backtracking in simple words.
Backtracking explores candidate solutions and reverses choices when a path cannot produce a valid solution. It is useful for permutations, combinations, Sudoku, and N-Queens.
Explain Bellman-Ford in simple words.
Bellman-Ford computes single-source shortest paths and can detect reachable negative-weight cycles. It is useful for graphs that may contain negative edge weights.
Explain Dijkstra Algorithm in simple words.
Dijkstra's algorithm computes shortest paths from a source when edge weights are nonnegative. It is useful for shortest-route problems with nonnegative weights.
What should a beginner know about Hash Set?
A hash set stores unique values using hashing. Insertion, deletion, and membership checks are O(1) on average.
Give an interview-style explanation of Minimum Spanning Tree.

A minimum spanning tree connects all vertices of a connected weighted undirected graph with minimum total edge weight and no cycles. Kruskal's algorithm typically takes O(E log E). It is useful for designing low-cost networks.
Give a simple example of Two Pointers.
Pointers can move inward from both ends of a sorted array.
What should a beginner know about Sorting?
Sorting arranges elements according to a specified order. Merge sort and heap sort take O(n log n); quicksort has O(n log n) average time.
What is Prefix Sum?
A prefix sum stores cumulative sums of array elements.
What should a beginner know about Graph?
A graph consists of vertices connected by edges. Graph algorithm complexity depends on the representation and the operation.
When should we use Segment Tree?
It is useful for range-sum, minimum, maximum, and other associative range queries.
Explain the main idea behind Quick Sort.
Quicksort partitions elements around a pivot and recursively sorts the partitions. It is useful for general-purpose in-memory sorting.
Give a simple example of Queue.
Enqueue 10 and then 20. Dequeue returns 10 first.
What should a beginner know about Binary Search Tree?

A binary search tree orders keys so that left-subtree keys are smaller and right-subtree keys are larger, under the usual distinct-key convention. Search, insertion, and deletion take O(h), where h is the tree height.
Give an interview-style explanation of Bit Manipulation.

Bit manipulation operates directly on the binary representation of integers. Basic bitwise operations take O(1) time for fixed-width integers. It is useful for masks, flags, parity checks, and efficient state representation.

Time and space complexity depend on the recurrence and recursion depth.
When should we use Memoization?
It is useful for top-down dynamic programming.
Give a simple example of Dijkstra Algorithm.
If A-B costs 2 and B-C costs 3, the path A-B-C costs 5.
Give an interview-style explanation of Dynamic Programming.

Dynamic programming solves overlapping subproblems and stores their results to avoid repeated computation. Complexity depends on the number of states and transitions. It is useful for optimization and counting problems with suitable recurrence relations.
When should we use Fenwick Tree?
It is useful for dynamic prefix sums and frequency counting.
Give an interview-style explanation of Prefix Sum.
A prefix sum stores cumulative sums of array elements. Building prefix sums takes O(n), and range-sum queries take O(1). It is useful for answering repeated range-sum queries.
Give a simple example of Deque.
A deque can add 10 at the front and 20 at the back.

When should we use Merge Sort?
It is useful when predictable sorting performance is required.
Explain the main idea behind Trie.
A trie stores strings through shared prefixes in a tree-like structure. Tries are useful for autocomplete, dictionaries, and prefix searches.

Tree traversal visits the nodes of a tree in a specified order. Traversals are useful for processing hierarchical structures.

Standard traversals take O(n) time.

Give an interview-style explanation of Greedy Algorithm.

A greedy algorithm makes a locally optimal choice at each step. Complexity depends on the choices and any sorting or data structures used. It is useful when a problem has the greedy-choice property and optimal substructure.

A greedy algorithm makes a locally optimal choice at each step. It is useful when a problem has the greedy-choice property and optimal substructure.
When should we use Hash Set?
Hash sets are useful for duplicate detection and membership testing.
Give an interview-style explanation of Kadane Algorithm.
Kadane's algorithm finds the maximum-sum contiguous subarray in a one-dimensional array. Its time complexity is O(n) and auxiliary space can be O(1). It is useful for maximum subarray sum problems.

It is useful for maximum subarray sum problems.

A permutation algorithm chooses one unused element, recurses, and then removes that choice.

Partitioning [3, 1, 2] around a pivot rearranges elements by their relation to the pivot.
Give an interview-style explanation of Stack.
A stack follows LIFO, meaning Last In, First Out. Push, pop, and top are O(1) for a typical stack implementation. Stacks are useful for recursion, undo operations, and balanced parentheses.
When should we use Deque?
Deques are useful for sliding-window maximum problems.

Merge sort and heap sort take O(n log n); quicksort has O(n log n) average time.

Tree traversal visits the nodes of a tree in a specified order. Traversals are useful for processing hierarchical structures.
What should a beginner know about Backtracking?
Backtracking explores candidate solutions and reverses choices when a path cannot produce a valid solution. Its worst-case time is often exponential.

What is Hash Map?
A hash map stores key-value pairs using a hash function.
Explain Lowest Common Ancestor in simple words.
The lowest common ancestor is the deepest node that is an ancestor of two given nodes. It is useful for finding shared ancestry in trees.
Give an interview-style explanation of Binary Search.
Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search interval. Its time complexity is O(log n) on a sorted array. It is useful for searching sorted data and finding monotonic boundaries.
What is the time complexity associated with Memoization?
It can reduce exponential recursive algorithms to polynomial time when there are only polynomially many states and transitions.
When should we use Dijkstra Algorithm?
It is useful for shortest-route problems with nonnegative weights.
What should a beginner know about Stack?
A stack follows LIFO, meaning Last In, First Out. Push, pop, and top are O(1) for a typical stack implementation.
Give an interview-style explanation of Monotonic Stack.

A monotonic stack maintains elements in increasing or decreasing order. Many monotonic-stack algorithms run in O(n) because each element is pushed and popped at most once. It is useful for next-greater-element and histogram-area problems.
What is Trie?
A trie stores strings through shared prefixes in a tree-like structure.
Give an interview-style explanation of Trie.

A trie stores strings through shared prefixes in a tree-like structure. Searching for a word takes O(L), where L is the word length, ignoring implementation-specific costs. Tries are useful for autocomplete, dictionaries, and prefix searches.
Explain Hash Set in simple words.
A hash set stores unique values using hashing. Hash sets are useful for duplicate detection and membership testing.
What is the time complexity associated with Lowest Common Ancestor?
A standard binary-tree DFS solution takes O(n) time.
Explain Segment Tree in simple words.
A segment tree stores information about array intervals in a tree structure. It is useful for range-sum, minimum, maximum, and other associative range queries.
What is Fenwick Tree?
A Fenwick tree, also called a Binary Indexed Tree, maintains prefix aggregates efficiently.
Give a simple example of AVL Tree.
AVL rotations restore balance after an insertion makes a node unbalanced.
What should a beginner know about Merge Sort?
Merge sort divides an array, sorts the parts, and merges them. Its time complexity is O(n log n), with O(n) auxiliary space for arrays.
